les: Die seepad na Indië, en die skepe wat volg
kaps_punt: Die reis van Da Gama VOC (Hollandse Oos-Indiese Kompanjie) reise

items.bewering: Na Dias se reis het die seepad na die Ooste nog net halfpad geloop.
items.bron: Rough figure that holds. Dias's farthest point was Kwaaihoek near the Boesmans River, 12 March 1488 (SAHO, sahistory.org.za/people/bartolomeu-dias and sahistory.org.za/node/10799). Lisbon to the Cape is about 5 200 nautical miles by sea (Union-Castle table, Madeira-Cape 4 677 nmi, plus Lisbon-Funchal about 520 nmi, elucidariomadeirense.pt). From the Cape to India is at least 4 500 nmi even as straight lines (Cape Town-Mombasa great circle 2 145 nmi, airportdistancecalculator.com; Mombasa-Kochi great circle 2 360 nmi, 1flt.com), and longer along the coast. That puts Dias's route at a little over half the distance. Read as a figure of speech, 'halfpad' is fair. It should not be taught as an exact measurement.

items.bewering: Portugal wou weet of 'n skip die hele pad tot in Indië kon vaar.
items.bron: World History Encyclopedia, 'Vasco da Gama' (worldhistory.org/Vasco_da_Gama). The next voyage after Dias was planned to reach India, mainly for spices and for Christian allies. The lesson simplifies the motive to whether the route could be sailed. That is part of the real aim, so it is not false. The spice motive appears later in the lesson.

items.bewering: 'n Portugese vloot onder Vasco da Gama het toe verder as Dias gevaar.
items.bron: World History Encyclopedia, 'Vasco da Gama'. Four ships left Lisbon on 8 July 1497, rounded the Cape on 22 November 1497 and went on up the East African coast, far past Dias's turning point of 1488 (SAHO).

items.bewering: Hulle het om die suidpunt en toe noord langs die ooskus van Afrika gevaar.
items.bron: World History Encyclopedia, 'Vasco da Gama'. After the Cape and Mossel Bay the fleet sailed up the East African coast, calling at Quelimane, then Mombasa on 7 April and Malindi on 15 April 1498. Da Gama also passed Cape Agulhas, the true southernmost point, so 'om die suidpunt' holds on either reading.

items.bewering: Van daar het hulle oor die Indiese Oseaan gevaar.
items.bron: World History Encyclopedia, 'Vasco da Gama'. The fleet left Malindi on 24 April 1498 and crossed the Indian Ocean in about 23 days.

items.bewering: Hulle het by 'n handelstad aan die weskus van Indië aangekom.
items.bron: World History Encyclopedia, 'Vasco da Gama'. They arrived near Calicut (Kozhikode) on 18 May 1498. Calicut is a trading city on the Malabar coast, India's south-western coast. Sources give 18, 20 or 22 May, but the lesson gives no day.

items.bewering: Nou het 'n seepad van Europa om Afrika tot in Indië geloop.
items.bron: World History Encyclopedia, 'Vasco da Gama'. This was the first direct voyage from Portugal to India, which opened the Cape route.

items.bewering: Die Indiese Oseaan was nie 'n leë see nie.
items.blok: Hulle het nie in 'n leë see aangekom nie
items.bron: Mapping checked. 'Not an empty sea' stands for 'other people already sailed and traded here', and that is accurate (World History Encyclopedia: an established Indian Ocean trade led by Swahili-coast and Persian Gulf traders; EBSCO Research Starters, 'Portuguese reach the Swahili coast'). A learner reasoning further would conclude the Portuguese joined an existing system rather than finding a new one. That conclusion is correct.

items.bewering: Handelaars van Arabië, van Indië en van die Swahili-kus het al eeue lank hier gevaar.
items.blok: Hulle het nie in 'n leë see aangekom nie
items.bron: World History Encyclopedia, 'Vasco da Gama' (an established trade dominated by Swahili-coast and Persian Gulf traders, with Indian merchants at Calicut). EBSCO Research Starters and National Geographic Education, 'People of the coast' (monsoon trade linking the Swahili coast, Arabia and India, with Swahili city-states at their height from the 11th to the 16th century). Persians and others traded there too. The list is incomplete but not false.

items.bewering: Langs die kuste het hawens en stede gelê waar skepe hul vrag gelaai het.
items.blok: Hulle het nie in 'n leë see aangekom nie
items.bron: EBSCO Research Starters and National Geographic Education. Swahili port cities such as Kilwa, Mombasa, Malindi and Zanzibar loaded gold, ivory and other goods. World History Encyclopedia: Calicut was an Indian trading port.

items.bewering: Da Gama se vloot het by 'n hawe aan die ooskus van Afrika 'n loods aan boord geneem.
items.blok: Hulle het nie in 'n leë see aangekom nie
items.bron: World History Encyclopedia, 'Vasco da Gama'. At Malindi, da Gama was given a pilot and a chart for the crossing to India. The pilot's identity is disputed: the old claim that he was Ahmad ibn Majid has been disproved, and other accounts make him Gujarati. The lesson does not name him, which is the safe form and should stay that way.

items.bewering: Daardie loods het die pad oor die oseaan geken en die skepe reg gewys.
items.blok: Hulle het nie in 'n leë see aangekom nie
items.bron: World History Encyclopedia, 'Vasco da Gama'. The pilot's knowledge of Indian Ocean conditions brought the fleet to Calicut in about 23 days.

items.bewering: Die see was dus aan ander mense goed bekend voordat die Portugese daar aangekom het.
items.blok: Hulle het nie in 'n leë see aangekom nie
items.bron: Follows from the two items above. World History Encyclopedia: the Portuguese already knew of a well-established cross-ocean trade before they arrived.

items.bewering: Baie jare later het handelaars uit Nederland na die Ooste begin vaar.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Compagnie van Verre'. A company of Amsterdam merchants sent its first fleet under Cornelis de Houtman from Texel on 2 April 1595, about a century after da Gama. 'Baie jare later' is accurate.

items.bewering: Hulle het een groot maatskappy gevorm.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Dutch East India Company' and 'Compagnie van Verre'; World History Encyclopedia, 'Dutch East India Company'. In 1602 the States General merged the rival Dutch companies (the voorcompagnieën) into one company, chartered on 20 March 1602 with 6.4 million guilders in capital. It was large by any measure.

items.bewering: Ons noem dit die VOC (Hollandse Oos-Indiese Kompanjie).
items.bron: The abbreviation is certain. VOC stands for Vereenigde Oostindische Compagnie, which is Verenigde Oos-Indiese Kompanjie in Afrikaans (af.wikipedia.org, 'Verenigde Oos-Indiese Kompanjie'; Dictionary of South African English, dsae.co.za, entry 'VOC'). Its usual English name is the Dutch East India Company. The bracketed name is what I cannot settle. I found no reference source that uses 'Hollandse Oos-Indiese Kompanjie': not Afrikaans Wikipedia (no article or redirect), not DSAE, not the Afrikaans history articles I searched. The only place I met it is the CAPS heading this lesson carries in its own kaps_punt. It reads as a translation of 'Dutch East India Company', which is a legitimate name for the company. But the bracket comes straight after the letters, so it reads as what V-O-C stands for, and the first letter does not match. A learner asked what VOC stands for would answer wrongly. A person should decide whether to keep the curriculum's name as it is, give the real expansion (Verenigde Oos-Indiese Kompanjie) and call the curriculum's name something it is also known as, or keep the abbreviation with the established name only. I have not marked it contradicted, because the name is the curriculum's own and is not false as a description.

items.bewering: Die VOC het jaar na jaar vlote om die suidpunt van Afrika na die Ooste gestuur.
items.bron: vocwarfare.net, 'The decision-making process and the rhythm of the return fleet'. The VOC sent outward fleets every year: a Christmas fleet and an Easter fleet, with a Kermis fleet added in the 1630s. Cultural Heritage Agency of the Netherlands, MaSS (mass.cultureelerfgoed.nl): two or more fleets a year to Asia.

items.bewering: Op 'n lang reis het die vars kos en water aan boord opgeraak.
items.bron: SAHO, 'Dutch settlement, the Indian Ocean slave trade and slavery at the Cape'. Ships sailed for months between Europe and the East, and many sailors died of scurvy, which comes from a lack of vitamin C, i.e. no fresh food.

items.bewering: Daarom het hulle skepe in Tafelbaai by die Kaap stilgehou vir vars water en kos.
items.bron: SAHO (same article). The VOC set up a station at the Cape so that fruit and vegetables could be grown for its sailors, and ships took on fresh water and food there. Britannica, 'Table Bay': the fresh water made it a stopping place. Afrikaans Wikipedia, 'Verenigde Oos-Indiese Kompanjie': Dutch and English ships stopped regularly in Table Bay even before the 1652 refreshment station. The lesson gives no date, so the sentence holds both before and after 1652.

items.bewering: Die Kaap lê aan die suidweste van Afrika.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Cape Peninsula' and 'Cape Point'. The Cape Peninsula, which holds Cape Town and Table Bay, sits at the south-western extremity of Africa. Note that the lesson rightly says south-west for the Cape and keeps 'suidpunt' for rounding the continent. The southernmost point is Cape Agulhas, and the lesson does not equate the Cape with the southern tip.

items.bewering: Eers het Dias om die suidpunt van Afrika en 'n entjie verder langs die kus gevaar.
items.blok: In watter orde dit gebeur het
items.bron: SAHO, 'Bartolomeu Dias' and '12 March 1488'. Dias rounded the southern end of Africa in 1488. He passed it out at sea, landed at Mossel Bay, and set up his last padrão at Kwaaihoek before turning back around the Boesmans, Great Fish or Keiskamma River (sources differ on the exact turning point). 'Eers' is true within the lesson's three-step order, and Dias is the first European on record to round the southern tip. 'n Entjie verder' fits the few hundred kilometres he went past it. The lesson names no river, which avoids the disputed detail.

items.bewering: In die 1490's het Da Gama toe die hele pad tot in Indië gevaar.
items.blok: In watter orde dit gebeur het
items.bron: World History Encyclopedia, 'Vasco da Gama'. He left Lisbon on 8 July 1497 and reached Calicut in May 1498. Both dates fall in the 1490s.

items.bewering: Baie later het VOC-vlote gereeld om die suidpunt van Afrika na die Ooste gevaar.
items.blok: In watter orde dit gebeur het
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Dutch East India Company' (founded 1602); vocwarfare.net (yearly fleets). This came about a century after da Gama, so the order and 'baie later' are correct.

items.bewering: Skepe uit Europa kon nou self speserye en ander goedere in die Ooste gaan haal.
items.bron: World History Encyclopedia, 'Vasco da Gama'. The route gave Portugal direct access to eastern goods, cut out middlemen and let Europeans into the eastern spice trade. The same source notes that the old overland routes to the Mediterranean did not end. The lesson does not say they did.

items.bewering: Vroeër het min skepe uit Europa tot by die suidpunt gekom.
items.bron: Checked against SAHO (Dias, 1488) and World History Encyclopedia (da Gama). Before the route opened, the only European ships known to have reached the southern tip were Dias's small fleet in 1488. 'Min' is accurate for the time before da Gama, which is what 'vroeër' points back to here. For the time before Dias the number is zero, but the lesson has already placed Dias first, so it does not suggest earlier European ships.

items.bewering: Nou het die pad om Suider-Afrika 'n gereelde skeepspad geword.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Portuguese India Armadas' (Carreira da Índia). Portugal sent armadas to India every year after da Gama, with 1 033 ship departures from Lisbon between 1497 and 1650. The VOC's yearly fleets followed later (vocwarfare.net).

items.bewering: VOC: Die groot maatskappy uit Nederland wat skepe na die Ooste gestuur het.
items.bron: Wikipedia and World History Encyclopedia, 'Dutch East India Company'. A Dutch company founded in 1602 to trade in Asia, which sent ships there every year. The definition is simple and true.

items.bewering: loods: Iemand wat die see goed ken en 'n skip se pad wys.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Maritime pilot': a mariner with special knowledge of local waters who guides ships through them. World History Encyclopedia: the Malindi pilot guided da Gama across the ocean. The definition fits both the modern and the historical sense used in this lesson.

items.bewering: vloot: 'n Groep skepe wat saamhoort: hulle het een eienaar, een leier of een soort werk.
items.bron: Merriam-Webster and American Heritage (via Wordnik), 'fleet': warships under one command, or vessels owned or run as one unit, e.g. fishing boats. Vocabulary.com: any group of ships sailing together. One owner, one leader or one kind of work maps onto these three senses. I could not reach an Afrikaans dictionary (Viva WAT returned 404), so this rests on English dictionaries for the shared concept.

opsomming: Every claim about Dias, da Gama, the Indian Ocean traders, the VOC fleets and Table Bay checks out, but a person must decide on one naming item: the lesson glosses VOC as 'Hollandse Oos-Indiese Kompanjie', a name that appears in no reference source I could find (only in the curriculum heading this lesson carries) and that does not match the letters, which stand for Verenigde Oos-Indiese Kompanjie, so a learner asked what VOC stands for would answer wrongly.
